name: Rood's Brown
lede: Rood's Brown is a warm, mid-toned brown from Robert Ridgway's 1912 color standards, also recorded as Wood Rose in Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, and no book we hold says who Rood was.

sections.title: A name the books leave open
sections.body:
Ridgway catalogued this brown on plate XXVIII of his 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary lists the same color under a different name, Wood Rose, first recorded in 1926 on their plate 6 [1]. No book we hold explains who Rood was, or whether the two names share a common source [1][2].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[sandalwood|Sandalwood]], about 2.5 units away, close to the paler [[sepia]] [3].

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: Measured in LCH terms it sits at lightness 47, chroma 22, hue 56 degrees, a warm, medium brown leaning toward red rather than yellow [3]. Next to [[sepia]] it reads as the pinker, less grey one, and sits between that and the paler [[pale-brown|Pale Brown]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brown, as photographed, in 1,644 of 23,781 paintings, about 6.9 percent [4]. It covers almost three-quarters of the canvas in a tenth-century Chinese ink painting, *Snow Plum*, and over 60 percent in a 1618 Mughal portrait of Raja Jagat Singh [4]. The earliest dated match is an ancient Egyptian funerary papyrus, where it covers 45 percent of the surviving fragment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. It sits closer to this warm red-brown than to the yellower [[beige-brown|Beige Brown]] [3]. These are computed color matches on aged, varnished or painted surfaces, not pigment identifications [4].
